svg.text: Fig. M3 — The field of H₂'s four magnets, in a plane through the bond (bond vertical)
field lines (contours of ρA_φ); shading = spin density; ring at 1 a0 coloured by the sign of B_r (orange N, blue S); arrows = the magnetic moments (orange)
electrons cancel; two proton dipoles of 0.0015 μB
the two electron spins, −2.0 μB in all
Long arrows, beside the axis: electron spin moments (opposite to the spins, the electron being negative). Short arrows, on the axis: proton moments (drawn
far larger than their 1/658 share). In the bound singlet only the protons remain, and the para form (proton spins opposite) has no field at all.
Zones round the molecule (Fig. M4): ortho protons alone show four zones between 0.3 and 1.6 a0 — two dipoles end to end, each 658 times weaker than one
electron's. With the triplet electrons the field is one pair at every radius except a thin shell round the protons (0.6–0.8 a0).
